events.title: The Compass Program
events.description:
Find Your Direction, Grow Your Skills,  Strengthen Your Impact

Every career has a moment when someone chooses to grow. To step into new challenges, understand themselves more deeply, and build skills that create real impact. The Compass Program gives professionals across Medina County the space to do exactly that.
This new professional development experience, created by the Greater Medina Chamber of Commerce and presented in partnership with the Heart to Heart Leadership, brings together personal growth, practical skills, and community connection.
Participants gain tools to understand themselves, communicate with confidence, support well-being, and engage with the community in meaningful ways. It is designed for professionals at every level, from rising talent to seasoned contributors who want to sharpen their skills and expand their influence.
Seats for the second class are limited. If you want yourself or your team to be part of something meaningful from the very start, now is the time to enroll.

Program Overview
The Compass Program includes five interactive sessions held September through December. All sessions take place at the Chamber office.
Participants do not just attend classes. They experience a guided journey shaped by local leaders, intentional conversation, and hands on skill building.
Each of the sessions includes a Foundational Skill Business Application, presented by a local Medina-area leader who brings the topic to life through real experience.

For a list of the Session dates, click HERE!

Who Should Attend
The Compass Program is designed for:
New professionals building strong foundations
Mid-level staff ready for growth
Experienced contributors wanting to deepen skills
Team members employers want to invest in

It is open to all who want to reflect, learn, connect, and bring new energy to their work and community.

For more information about the Program Objectives and Topics, click HERE!

events.title: Safety Council Meeting - September 2026
events.description:
MEETING TOPIC: HEALTHY BACKS & BODIES™ for The Keyboard Commando: Ergonomics That Work
Work doesn’t have to hurt. Discover how to dial in your workstation, correctly position your body, outsmart desk discomfort, and build simple habits that help you - and your employees - work better, feel better, and perform your best.

Talking Points:
The Big Three of Your Desk Environment: Mastering Monitor, Workstation, and Chair Setup
Guided Ergonomic Self-Assessment: Make Your Body and Your Space Work for You with Proper Alignment
Positioning for Laptops, Handheld Devices, Sitting, Standing, and Walking at Your Desk
Micro-Break Interventions to Improve Fluidity, Oxygenation, Mobility, Efficiency, and Productivity

Bio:
Tanya (Weiker) Snowden is the HEALTHY BACKS & BODIES™ Program Creator, Master Instructor, Safety Consultant, and Back Health Specialist. She is a Sports-Orthopedic Physical Therapist, Certified Ergonomics Assessment Specialist (CEAS), Advanced Office Ergonomics Assessment Specialist (AOEAS), Remote Ergonomics Assessment Specialist (REAS), JFB-MFR Clinician, and patented inventor of the TheraBand® CLX, as well as a published author.
‘If only I had known this sooner…’
During her time as an Orthopedic SportsHealth Spine Specialist at The Cleveland Clinic, it was this sentiment, frequently shared with Tanya by her ‘back’ patients as she taught them how to re-train and re-store proper body positions and the underlying biomechanics innate to safe, healthy, efficient movement, that eventually catapulted her out into the injury prevention training arena. Knowing that much of this pain & dysfunction, and many of these injuries, were preventable if only people knew how to inhabit their bodies and move them correctly, Tanya created HEALTHY BACKS & BODIES™ to reach a larger audience and to reach them ahead of time.
Her programs are the culmination of 30 years of hands-on treating, clinical insight, clinical and corporate teaching, and her intense drive to empower people and corporations to take action before the pain and dysfunction show themselves. She teaches and consults with the conviction and passion that can only come from an authentic love for the subject matter and from one who lives it every day.

events.title: FY27 Safety Council Enrollment or Renewal 2026-2027 Rebate Program
events.description:
Now is the time to JOIN the FY27 Medina County Safety Council.
Be a part of the 100+ companies that benefit from all safety council membership has to offer! Participation is simpler and easier than ever before.
Discover the power of Collaboration, Innovation and Networking!
Collaborate with local resources to develop prevention strategies and techniques that will enhance the safety of your workforce.
How can participating in Safety Council benefit you?
Learn techniques for increasing safety, health and wellness in your workplace.
Network and collaborate with other employers in your community to share best practices.
Learn about resources that can assist you in your accident prevention efforts.
Discover new and innovative safety techniques.

Participation made simple.
Join the Medina County Safety Council by September 30, 2026.
To qualify for a rebate, employers must earn a minimum of 10 Safety Council credits during the fiscal year. Credits can be earned through the following methods.
1. Safety council meeting attendance
Employers must be enrolled with the safety council whose meeting they are attending to earn meeting credit.

One credit per month may be earned by attending their safety council’s monthly meeting.

2. External training credits
Employers may earn a combined maximum of two credits per fiscal year by attending approved external training sessions from any of the below options.
This includes:
BWC Safety Training Courses (in-person or virtual training course [VTC] only) One credit per course, with a maximum of two credits.

Safety training courses from external providers (in-person only)Examples include industry associations, third party administrators, or other sources approved by SCA. See External Training Guide for Sponsors.
One credit per course, with a maximum of two credits.

Annual Ohio Safety Congress & Expo® (OSC®)One credit may be earned for each day of in-person attendance, with a maximum of two credits per policy number, during the three-day event.

3. BWC on-site safety consultation
Employers may earn two credits for completing one BWC on-site safety consultation visit, limited to once every three fiscal years.

The consultation must be conducted by a BWC Field Safety Consultant, e.g., Industrial Safety Consultant, Industrial Hygienist, and/or Ergonomist, and include a full hazard assessment and a BWC claims review.

Key attendance credit guidelines:
Any representative of the employer qualifies for credit.
A person can represent only one policy number for credit.
Multiple representatives from the same employer attending a meeting, training, or special event count as one credit.
Employer participation in safety seminars, workshops, or conferences hosted or co-hosted by a safety council qualifies for one credit with a certificate.
Monthly meetings do not qualify for credit for employers not enrolled in that safety council.

Membership in the Medina County Safety Council is open to all businesses in the Medina County area, both large and small. It is sponsored by the BWC Division of Safety & Hygiene in cooperation with the Greater Medina Chamber of Commerce.
ALL companies must register to participate in the FY27 BWC Rebate Program. Registration required for new AND past participants.

3 Membership Options for FY7 Safety Council Rebate Program
#1. $0 option - Members of the Greater Medina Chamber have their Safety Council Membership Fee Waived (Included with Chamber membership; however, completion of enrollment is still required)
#2. $100 option - Non-Medina Chamber Members' Safety Council Annual Membership Fee
#3. $345 option - Become a Greater Medina Chamber member & your Safety Council Membership Fee is Waived
This does not include the price for the monthly Safety Council meetings. Separate purchase required to attend meetings.

For more information and questions, contact safety@medinaohchamber.com or call (330) 723-8773.

events.title: Raising the Bar
events.description:
Topic: Health Benefits Without the Headache - A Practical Conversation for Employers
If your company’s health and pharmacy costs feel increasingly difficult to understand—or control—you’re not alone.
This practical educational session will help small and mid-sized employers prepare for benefit renewal season. We’ll explain today’s cost pressures in plain language, including the impact of newer medications such as GLP-1s, and share questions you may want to ask your broker or carrier.
You’ll leave with:
• A clearer understanding of what is driving benefit costs
• Practical questions to bring to your next renewal conversation
• An overview of options available to businesses of different sizes
• Greater confidence navigating benefits without becoming an expert
Bring your questions and gain useful information to help you approach your next benefits renewal with confidence.
There is no cost to attend. Chamber members and prospective members are welcome, and registration is preferred but not required.

About the Speaker:
Don Hicks brings over 25 years of experience across legal, technology, and Human Capital Management, giving him a well-rounded perspective on how businesses operate and grow. Today, he serves as an Area Vice President with Vensure Employer Solutions, where he leads a team focused on helping organizations streamline HR processes and make smarter use of HR technology. He holds a master’s degree in public administration from Villanova University and is also a proud U.S. Marine Corps veteran, where he earned the distinguished honor of Marine of the Year. Outside of work, Don enjoys sports, movies, and reading about American history and business. He and his wife have been married for 25 years and live in Strongsville, Ohio with their son and their dog, Chloe.

events.title: Safety Council Meeting - October 2026
events.description:
MEETING TOPIC: The Next Frontier of Safety - Wellbeing & Suicide Prevention
For nearly 90 years, the construction industry has made tremendous strides in physical safety, dramatically reducing injuries and saving countless lives on job sites. However, a different crisis now demands our attention—one that claims even more lives than slips, trips, and falls: suicide. In this 45-minute presentation, you will learn practical strategies your company can implement to address these statistics and build a proactive culture of care.

Bio: Paul Lawson holds a bachelor’s degree from Cincinnati Christian University and has over ten years of experience in ministry. He combines his passion for wellness with his work in the construction industry in central Ohio, where he is a respected advocate for mental health and suicide prevention.
A two-time cancer survivor who has navigated his own mental health journey, Paul brings both lived experience and professional expertise to his work. After developing a comprehensive mental health program for a local contractor, he founded Paul Lawson Helps LLC to expand this impact across the industry.
Paul serves on the board of the Construction Industry Alliance for Suicide Prevention and is dedicated to fostering a culture of care in blue-collar industries through training, speaking, and advocacy.

He holds a master’s degree in public administration from Villanova University and is also a proud U.S. Marine Corps veteran, where he earned the distinguished honor of Marine of the Year. Outside of work, Don enjoys sports, movies, and reading about American history and business. He and his wife have been married for 25 years and live in Strongsville, Ohio with their son and their dog, Chloe.

events.title: Safety Council Meeting - April 2027
events.description:
MEETING TOPIC: The Foundation of Workplace Safety - Why Foot Health Matters
Foot health is a critical but often overlooked factor in workplace safety, especially for employees who spend long hours standing or walking. Poor footwear, hard surfaces, and fatigue can lead to injuries like slips, falls, and chronic pain, all of which impact productivity and increase costs. Simple changes like proper footwear policies, ergonomic improvements, and regular movement can significantly reduce these risks. Investing in foot health isn’t just about comfort; it’s a practical, cost-effective way to prevent injuries and strengthen overall workplace performance.
